overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance data clearly indicates that space exploration and planetary 'what-if' anomaly scenarios (published within the last 7 days) are dominating traction, achieving the highest views-per-day and robust like-to-view ratios (e.g., Venus, liquid diamond planets, and extreme cosmic environments). Older historical, general psychology, and animal facts published beyond 7 days show significantly lower velocity. Engagement concentrates heavily on exotic, visually striking astrophysics concepts presented via direct curiosity gaps.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (968 views), 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1024 views), and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) generated the highest absolute views and engagement rates within the recent 7-day window.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-concept astrophysical 'what-if' scenarios involving extreme physical environments, unusual planetary mechanics, and rare cosmic materials.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1026 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (825 views) performed exceptionally well among recent uploads.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more shorts focused on light-devouring anomalies, mysterious deep-space entities, and lesser-known extreme exoplanets.

weak_patterns.pattern: Older General Psychology & Standard Animal Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos older than 7 days dealing with standard psychological tricks or basic animal trivia (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Octopuses Have Three Hearts') plateaued quickly with minimal daily velocity and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard evergreen fact loops unless framed through an aggressive, high-stakes narrative or newly uncovered scientific anomaly.
